reuse.why: Extends the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds a shared isWeekendOrHoliday predicate used by every site, but the daily-vs-move decision (skipWeekend && frequency === 'daily') is rebuilt at each call site rather than owned by a shared function.

duplication.why: The daily-skip/else-shift decision is written in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template (as its negation movesWeekend), and getDatesInRange repeats getUpcomingDates' RSchedule/try/captureBreadcrumb and over-fetch scaffolding.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday predicates sit in shared/schedules.ts as they should, but the policy deciding skip vs move lives in server handlers and the budget template instead of next to them.

scope.why: Focused on schedule dates, the new handler, types and tests; three release notes for the steps are mild noise.

maintainability.why: The rule is spread across four sites with different spellings, and schedule-template now steers getNextDate by passing movesWeekend as its noSkipWeekend argument, an opaque coupling that a maintainer must understand to change the rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts), getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and createScheduleList (budget/schedule-template.ts) each decide daily weekend skipping around getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily rule appears as skipsWeekendDays in three functions and as its negation movesWeekend in schedule-template.ts; getDatesInRange reshapes getUpcomingDates' map/filter pipeline as a for-loop.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a holidays parameter; the daily-frequency special case is kept outside it at getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's createScheduleList.
